questions.q: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows $\langle2,1\rangle$ and $\langle3,-1\rangle$, and $B$ be the matrix with rows $\langle-1,4\rangle$ and $\langle0,2\rangle$. Find $A+B$ and $3A$.
questions.answer: $A+B$ has rows $\langle1,5\rangle$ and $\langle3,1\rangle$. $3A$ has rows $\langle6,3\rangle$ and $\langle9,-3\rangle$.

questions.q: Using the same $A$ and $B$, find $A-2B$.
Using $A$ (rows $\langle2,1\rangle$, $\langle3,-1\rangle$) and $B$ (rows $\langle-1,4\rangle$, $\langle0,2\rangle$) from above, find $AB$.
questions.answer: $AB$ has rows $\langle-2,10\rangle$ and $\langle-3,10\rangle$: e.g. row $1$, column $1$ is $(2)(-1)+(1)(0)=-2$.

questions.q: Let $A$ have rows $\langle2,1\rangle$ and $\langle3,-1\rangle$, and let $\mathbf{v}=\langle2,-3\rangle$. Find $A\mathbf{v}$.
Explain, without computing $BA$, why $AB$ and $BA$ need not be equal for $2\times2$ matrices.
questions.answer: Matrix multiplication combines rows of the first factor with columns of the second; swapping the order pairs different rows with different columns, so in general $AB \neq BA$ (matrix multiplication is not commutative).

questions.q: Find $\det A$ for the matrix $A$ with rows $\langle2,1\rangle$ and $\langle3,-1\rangle$, and state whether $A$ is invertible.
Find $A^{-1}$ for the matrix $A$ with rows $\langle2,1\rangle$ and $\langle3,-1\rangle$.
questions.answer: $A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{-5}\times$ the matrix with rows $\langle-1,-1\rangle$ and $\langle-3,2\rangle$, i.e., $A^{-1}$ has rows $\langle0.2,0.2\rangle$ and $\langle0.6,-0.4\rangle$.

questions.q: Without computing it, explain why the matrix with rows $\langle4,2\rangle$ and $\langle6,3\rangle$ has no inverse.
questions.answer: $\det = (4)(3)-(2)(6) = 12-12 = 0$, and a matrix with determinant $0$ has no inverse (Theorem 2.1).

questions.q: Solve the system $3x-y=8$ and $x+2y=5$ using $\mathbf{x}=M^{-1}\mathbf{b}$.
questions.answer: $M$ has rows $\langle3,-1\rangle$ and $\langle1,2\rangle$, so $\det M=(3)(2)-(-1)(1)=7$, and $M^{-1}$ has rows $\langle\frac{2}{7},\frac{1}{7}\rangle$ and $\langle-\frac{1}{7},\frac{3}{7}\rangle$. Then $x=\frac{1}{7}\left[2(8)+1(5)\right]=3$ and $y=\frac{1}{7}\left[-1(8)+3(5)\right]=1$. Check: $3(3)-1=8$ and $3+2(1)=5$.

questions.q: For $\mathbf{u}=\langle3,4\rangle$ and $\mathbf{w}=\langle-4,3\rangle$, find $\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{w}$ and $|\mathbf{u}|$.
What does $\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{w}=0$ tell you about $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{w}$ from the previous question?
questions.answer: A zero dot product means $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{w}$ are perpendicular (orthogonal).

questions.q: Find $A^{-1}$ for the matrix $A$ with rows $\langle3,1\rangle$ and $\langle-1,0\rangle$.
questions.answer: $\det A=(3)(0)-(1)(-1)=1$. $A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{1}\times$ the matrix with rows $\langle0,-1\rangle$ and $\langle1,3\rangle$, giving rows $\langle0,-1\rangle$ and $\langle1,3\rangle$.

questions.q: Find $A^{-1}$ for the matrix $A$ with rows $\langle2,1\rangle$ and $\langle3,1\rangle$.
questions.answer: $\det A=(2)(1)-(1)(3)=-1$. $A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{-1}\times$ the matrix with rows $\langle1,-1\rangle$ and $\langle-3,2\rangle$, giving rows $\langle-1,1\rangle$ and $\langle3,-2\rangle$.

questions.q: Find $A^{-1}$ for the matrix $A$ with rows $\langle1,-2\rangle$ and $\langle2,-5\rangle$.
questions.answer: $\det A=(1)(-5)-(-2)(2)=-1$. $A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{-1}\times$ the matrix with rows $\langle-5,2\rangle$ and $\langle-2,1\rangle$, giving rows $\langle5,-2\rangle$ and $\langle2,-1\rangle$.

questions.q: Find $A^{-1}$ for the matrix $A$ with rows $\langle2,1\rangle$ and $\langle-5,-3\rangle$.
questions.answer: $\det A=(2)(-3)-(1)(-5)=-1$. $A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{-1}\times$ the matrix with rows $\langle-3,-1\rangle$ and $\langle5,2\rangle$, giving rows $\langle3,1\rangle$ and $\langle-5,-2\rangle$.

questions.q: Solve the system $6y=-30$ and $6x=24$ using $\mathbf{x}=M^{-1}\mathbf{b}$.
questions.answer: $M$ has rows $\langle0,6\rangle$ and $\langle6,0\rangle$, so $\det M=(0)(0)-(6)(6)=-36$. Solving gives $x=4$ and $y=-5$. Check: $(0)(4)-30=-30$ and $(6)(4)=24$.

questions.q: Solve the system $4x-5y=-3$ and $-6x+4y=-6$ using $\mathbf{x}=M^{-1}\mathbf{b}$.
questions.answer: $M$ has rows $\langle4,-5\rangle$ and $\langle-6,4\rangle$, so $\det M=(4)(4)-(-5)(-6)=-14$. Solving gives $x=3$ and $y=3$. Check: $(4)(3)-15=-3$ and $(-6)(3)+12=-6$.

questions.q: Solve the system $x+3y=-15$ and $x+2y=-8$ using $\mathbf{x}=M^{-1}\mathbf{b}$.
questions.answer: $M$ has rows $\langle1,3\rangle$ and $\langle1,2\rangle$, so $\det M=(1)(2)-(3)(1)=-1$. Solving gives $x=6$ and $y=-7$. Check: $(1)(6)-21=-15$ and $(1)(6)-14=-8$.

questions.q: Solve the system $2x-y=5$ and $6x+6y=-48$ using $\mathbf{x}=M^{-1}\mathbf{b}$.
questions.answer: $M$ has rows $\langle2,-1\rangle$ and $\langle6,6\rangle$, so $\det M=(2)(6)-(-1)(6)=18$. Solving gives $x=-1$ and $y=-7$. Check: $(2)(-1)+7=5$ and $(6)(-1)-42=-48$.

questions.q: Solve the system $x-y=0$ and $-3x-6y=-54$ using $\mathbf{x}=M^{-1}\mathbf{b}$.
questions.answer: $M$ has rows $\langle1,-1\rangle$ and $\langle-3,-6\rangle$, so $\det M=(1)(-6)-(-1)(-3)=-9$. Solving gives $x=6$ and $y=6$. Check: $(1)(6)-6=0$ and $(-3)(6)-36=-54$.
